Hi Anna — really appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a first-pass proposal and a payment schedule that illustrates the options you asked about. High-level summary below, followed by the attachment details.

Summary (numbers illustrative):
- Option A — Annual Prepay (single invoice per year): 20% list discount on hosted rates, annual invoice due Net-60.
- Option B — 3‑Year Prepay (committed spend, billed upfront for year 1, then annual billing for years 2–3): 27% effective discount across three years if paid as: 40% upfront (year 1), 30% at start of year 2, 30% at start of year 3 — default invoices Net-30.
- Option C — 3‑Year Prepay with milestone invoices (preferred by our finance team): 25% effective discount with partial upfront (30% at signing), then quarterly milestone invoices (20%/20%/15%/15% for year 1) and yearly thereafter; Net-60 for milestone invoices if customer provides a single-signature prepay agreement.

Payment-term exceptions we can consider: Net-90 is atypical for prepay, but we will consider Net-90 if the customer accepts: a) an increased escrow holdback, or b) a larger upfront percentage (e.g., 50% upfront) or c) milestone-based irrevocable payment schedule via PO. We'll need finance approval for any Net-90 exception.

Attachments:
- CuroHealth_Tiered_Prepay_Proposal_v2.pdf (proposal, 168KB) — includes line-item pricing, SLA language, and a 3-year ramp scenario with token buckets.
- CuroHealth_Payment_Schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet, 24KB) — shows invoice dates, amounts, and sample amortization.

If you'd like, we can iterate on this table and I can loop in our finance lead for sign-off.

Best,

Grace / Rishi — Finance looked at the illustrative schedules. Notes from FP&A:

- Net-90 is low-margin risk unless secured. For milestone model we can accept Net-90 only if: 1) the first milestone is >= 35% and is paid within 30 days of invoice; AND 2) CuroHealth provides a signed purchase order referencing Redwood's payment terms and an irrevocable bank guarantee for outstanding amounts > 90 days.
- If they insist on Net-90 without guarantees, money operations will require a 50% upfront prepay for year 1 (we can offer 22–24% discount for that structure).
- For bookkeeping simplicity, Finance prefers an annual reconciliation invoice for usage true-up rather than many small micro-invoices each month — suggest quarterly milestones capped to four invoices in year 1.

If Legal signs off on the guarantee language, I'm comfortable recommending Option C with conditional Net-90. We'll need Sales to capture signatures and the PO before routing to finance for final approval.

-Monica
